name: Sulfamethoxazole and trimethoprim
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero

usual_adult_dose.dose: 800/160 mg (1 DS tablet) every 12 hours; 10 to 14 days (UTI) or 5 days (shigellosis)
Sulfamethoxazole 75 to 100 mg/kg and trimethoprim 15 to 20 mg/kg per day in divided doses every 6 hours for 14 to 21 days

key_interactions.drug_or_class: ACE inhibitors, ARBs, spironolactone and other potassium-raising drugs

key_interactions.effect: Higher free methotrexate; bone marrow suppression (label).

key_interactions.action: Avoid concurrent use; monitor creatinine if needed.

serious: Severe skin reactions (Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis, DRESS)
Acute kidney injury, interstitial nephritis, crystalluria
Bone marrow suppression, thrombocytopenia, hemolytic anemia

contraindications: Drug-induced immune thrombocytopenia with either component
Severe renal insufficiency when renal function cannot be monitored

pk.half_life: Sulfamethoxazole about 10 hours; trimethoprim 8 to 10 hours
pk.excretion_renal_pct: Total sulfonamide 84.5% and free trimethoprim 66.8% in urine within 72 hours
pk.dialyzability: Moderate by hemodialysis; not by peritoneal dialysis (label)
